IBMCEPH-14046.analysis:
SUMMARY: `ceph orch ls --export` outputs ingress ssl_cert as a single-line quoted string instead of YAML multiline (|), causing certificate corruption when the exported YAML is re-applied.

ROOT CAUSE:
The cephadm service spec export code serializes the ssl_cert field as a regular YAML string (single-line with quotes) instead of using the YAML block scalar indicator (|) for multiline content. When this exported YAML is fed back into `ceph orch apply`, the certificate newlines are lost, producing a corrupted certificate that HAProxy cannot use. The fix ensures ssl_cert is always serialized with the YAML multiline block indicator.

KEY EVIDENCE:
- `ceph orch ls --export` outputs: `ssl_cert: '---BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY---...` (single line)
- Expected: `ssl_cert: |\n    -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----` (multiline)
- Reproducible always
- Workaround: manually edit YAML to add multiline indicator
- Fix merged downstream: gitlab.cee.redhat.com/ceph/ceph/-/merge_requests/1753
- Verified in 9.0z3 build 20.1.0-205

FIX STATUS:
- Status: Closed (GA in 9.0z3)
- Downstream MR 1753 merged. Verified working in build 20.1.0-205.

IBMCEPH-14079.analysis:
SUMMARY: RGW multisite sync fails with lock lease failure on buckets with 100-600M objects during full sync.
ROOT CAUSE: During bucket full sync of very large buckets (100-600M objects), multiple RGW instances compete for the bucket-wide lease required by RGWContinuousLeaseCR. The lock acquisition fails with retcode=-16 (EBUSY), preventing any single instance from maintaining sync progress. This is exacerbated when multiple large buckets share the same datalog shards, creating a 'sync storm' where buckets block each other. The full sync never transitions to incremental sync because no instance can hold the lock long enough to complete the listing.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- Log: 'RGWContinuousLeaseCR: couldn't lock sir-fbd.rgw.log:bucket.full-sync-status...:bucket sync: retcode=-16'

IBMCEPH-14098.analysis:
SUMMARY: RGW PUT/LIST performance degradation caused by 276M failed multipart uploads inflating bucket-index OMAP.
ROOT CAUSE: Failed/abandoned multipart uploads accumulate as OMAP entries in the bucket-index shards. With 725M total entries (508M regular + 217M orphaned multiparts) across 4999 shards (~145K entries/shard), the per-shard OMAP size far exceeds the recommended ~100K threshold. This causes RocksDB iterator depth increase, higher compaction frequency, more tombstone accumulation, and degraded read/write latency. A contributing BlueFS DB read stall (11 seconds on one host) was also observed. The application (Flink) abandons multipart uploads without aborting them.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- Customer: Apple (IBM Case TS022018591)
- 276M aborted multipart entries in single bucket
- Per-shard OMAP: ~145K entries/shard (target is ~100K)
- Environment: IBM Ceph 8.1z3 with HDD-backed pools
- Recommendation: LC cleanup with tuned workers + lifecycle policy to prevent recurrence
- Matthew Benjamin confirmed LC tuning numbers are realistic
- Performance collection script provided for before/after comparison
FIX STATUS: Operational guidance provided. Customer needs to: 1) Apply AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload LC policy, 2) Tune rgw_lc_max_worker/rgw_lc_max_wp_worker, 3) Fix Flink application to abort multipart uploads. Estimated cleanup: 3-14 days depending on throughput.

IBMCEPH-14114.analysis:
SUMMARY: Persistent CRC read errors on a single CephFS object (Jira queue file) that follow the PG across OSD moves. Not a Ceph bug -- the object data was genuinely corrupted.
ROOT CAUSE: A single CephFS object (inode 0x10002205622, a Jira application queue file) had corrupted data with mismatched CRC checksums. When the PG was moved from OSD.13 to OSD.35 to OSD.12, the CRC errors followed because the corruption was in the object data itself, not in the OSD hardware. The primary OSD consistently failed CRC verification because all replicas contained the same corrupted data (the corruption predated replication). Resolution: customer moved the corrupted file (`mv` to another location) which stopped the CRC errors, then deleted it.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- CRC mismatch: `full-object read crc 0x9be580fa != expected 0x942f10f9 on 1:a59dca4b:::10002205622.00000000:head`
- OSD_TOO_MANY_REPAIRS: osd.12 had 14993 reads repaired
- CRC errors followed PG from OSD.13 -> OSD.35 -> OSD.12 (all replicas corrupted)
- Object identified as CephFS inode for a Jira queue file
- Resolution: `mv` the file away, CRC errors stopped immediately
FIX STATUS: Closed as 'not a bug'. Object-level data corruption, not a Ceph defect. Customer will upgrade to latest 6.1z-stream.

IBMCEPH-14127.analysis:
SUMMARY: RocksDB logging at debug level 4/5 causes excessive /var/log/messages growth on OSD nodes.
ROOT CAUSE: The default debug_rocksdb=4/5 setting in shipped container images causes high-frequency log entries, particularly when combined with bluestore_rocksdb_options that configure multiple WAL buffers with per-buffer compression. Each compression event generates verbose RocksDB log output. The 4/5 notation means 'log at level 4 to memory, level 5 to disk' which is very verbose for production. The default was verified on 19.2.1-331.el9cp (8.1z5). The issue is environment-dependent -- clusters with heavy write workloads see significantly more log growth.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- Confirmed debug_rocksdb=4/5 is the upstream default (unchanged for years)
- Affected version: 16.2.10-275.el8cp (Ceph 5.3), also seen in Ceph 7
- Workaround exists: manually set logging to level 1/5
- bluestore_rocksdb_options configured with 4 WAL buffers of 256MB each, individually compressed
- Engineering requested specific log samples and growth rates to justify changing defaults
FIX STATUS: Status 'new'. Engineering is investigating whether the default should be lowered. Awaiting customer-provided log samples and growth rate data.

IBMCEPH-14151.analysis:
SUMMARY: Customer requests increasing osd_max_omap_entries_per_request from 1024 to 16384 for faster bucket-index OMAP scans.
ROOT CAUSE: The default osd_max_omap_entries_per_request (1024) limits how many OMAP entries an OSD returns per librados get_omap_vals call. For a custom application scanning 725M bucket-index entries across 4999 shards, this requires ~140 sequential round trips per shard. Raising to 16384 would reduce to ~9 RTTs per shard. The original default (131072) was lowered to 1024 in commit 3ca46da937d (2019) to cap misbehaving clients, not because OSDs can't handle larger responses. The trade-off is bandwidth vs latency: larger requests hold locks longer, potentially impacting p99 latency for concurrent small ops.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- Customer: Apple (IBM Case TS022020602)
- Bucket: 725M entries, 4999 shards, full scan takes 7.6 hours with 64 workers
- Engineering confirmed 16K is safe for NVMe-backed index pools
- Upstream PR: https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/70529
- Radosław confirmed: both osd_max_omap_entries_per_request and osd_max_omap_bytes_per_request are enforced at same places
- Recommended rollout: 4096 → 8192 → 16384 with monitoring
FIX STATUS: Upstream PR submitted (PR #70529). Target: Ceph 10.0 (was 11.0, moved back to 10.0 by Bipin Kunal).

IBMCEPH-14166.analysis:
SUMMARY: MON ms_dispatch thread consumes 100% CPU due to excessive LogClient::_get_mon_log_message() processing, likely caused by commit 22cd0d42a15 changing failed auth handling from silent ignore to explicit reset processing.

ROOT CAUSE:
After upgrading from Ceph 6.1 (Quincy 17.2.6) to 8.1 (Squid 19.2.1), MON peon CPU increases dramatically. Commit 22cd0d42a15 changed failed authentication handling: in 6.1, a failed auth returned an ignored integer and the connection continued silently; in 8.1, the return type changed to bool -- a failure now returns false, causing handle_auth_request to return -EACCES and triggering ms_handle_reset on the dispatch path. In a cluster with ~1,300 connections/min, this additional per-connection reset processing (ms_handle_reset per connection increased +50%, _assign_global_id per connection +45%) accumulates on the dispatch thread, causing MON CPU to reach 100%.

KEY EVIDENCE:
- perf top ms_dispatch: `LogClient::_get_mon_log_message()` = 75.9% of CPU
- ms_handle_reset per connection: 12.1 (6.1) -> 18.1 (8.1) = +50%
- Commit identified: https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/ceph/ceph/-/commit/22cd0d42a15e19d9ca3b6bd99e108993d3fd2263
- Workaround: `clog_to_monitors false` temporarily reduces load but impacts monitoring
- Only MON peon CPUs affected (leader unchanged); correlated with memory increase
- Aarti Dhikale: working on build with reverted changes for testing

FIX STATUS:
- Status: Assigned (under active investigation)
- Root cause commit identified; fix build with revert being prepared
- Workaround: `ceph config set global clog_to_monitors false` (impacts monitoring)

IBMCEPH-14176.analysis:
SUMMARY: Custom Acadia MGR plugin experiences delays during OSD slow ops because RBD/RADOS operations go directly to OSDs, not cached MGR data.
ROOT CAUSE: The Acadia (IBM Cloud) MGR plugin uses RADOS/RBD APIs (rbd.Image(), image.diff_iterate(), self.rados.open_ioctx()) which perform direct I/O to OSDs, unlike cached cluster maps (self.get('df'), self.get('osd_map')) which are served from MGR memory. During slow OSD operations, these direct I/O calls experience the same delays as client I/O. Additionally, the plugin encounters 'failed to retrieve initial metadata: (2) No such file or directory' for multiple RBD images, suggesting stale/deleted image references in the plugin's internal state or expired cache.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- Slow ops reported: 'get_health_metrics reporting 26 slow ops' for RBD read/write operations
- Multiple 'librbd::image::OpenRequest: failed to retrieve initial metadata: (2) No such file or directory' errors
- Plugin uses RBD/RADOS APIs that directly interact with OSDs
- L3 team determined the custom plugin issues are out of scope for Ceph engineering
- Customer's Acadia plugin source code access was not granted
FIX STATUS: Closed as 'not a bug'. Issue is in the custom Acadia MGR plugin, not in Ceph itself. Customer directed to contact Acadia plugin maintainers.

IBMCEPH-14312.analysis:
### Root Cause Analysis:
```
SUMMARY: OSD crashes with MOSDRepOp::encode_payload assertion failure due to messenger feature negotiation race
ROOT CAUSE: A known regression in Ceph Reef (18.2.1) where the msg/async layer encodes messages before connection features are fully negotiated. The assertion 'HAVE_FEATURE(features, SERVER_OCTOPUS)' fails in MOSDRepOp::encode_payload() when the message is encoded before the peer connection has advertised its feature set. This is a race condition in the messenger v2 protocol during connection establishment under high I/O load. The fix (upstream Reef PR #59286) ensures messages are encoded only after features are fully set. Fix already existed in 8.1z4+ but customer on 7.1z3 with OpenStack 17.1.4 couldn't upgrade to 8.x.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- Assertion: 'HAVE_FEATURE(features, SERVER_OCTOPUS)' in MOSDRepOp.h:127
- Stack: encode_payload -> send_message -> ReplicatedBackend::issue_op
- Version: 18.2.1-298.1.hotfix.bz2359773.el9cp
- Daily crashes, extreme IO load (172k IOPS, 6.5 GiB/s)
- Pool 'volumes' at 87% full, size=2/min_size=1
- BZ#2359773 tracking upstream
FIX STATUS: Fixed. Hotfix cherry-picked to 7.1z10 (18.2.1-381.0.hotfix.IBMCEPH14312). Testing complete, no regressions. Customer confirmed fix resolved the issue. Closed as part of 7.1z10.
```

IBMCEPH-14326.analysis:
SUMMARY: Procedure for replacing a healthy tiebreaker monitor with a new monitor in the same datacenter.
ROOT CAUSE: Documentation only describes replacing a failed tiebreaker monitor or adding a new arbiter. Customer needed to replace a healthy tiebreaker but the new monitor (added on a separate public network) didn't join quorum. The procedure was confirmed by engineering: spin up new monitor in tiebreaker site, wait for quorum join, use 'ceph mon set_new_tiebreaker' on the new monitor, then gracefully remove the old one with 'ceph orch daemon rm <old-monitor> --force'. The old tiebreaker remains disallowed from being leader until explicitly removed.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- Version: IBM Storage Ceph 6.1z2 [17.2.6-148.el9cp]
- 2 public networks defined; new monitor on separate network from existing tiebreaker
- Engineering confirmed: ceph orch daemon rm uses 'ceph mon rm' under the hood (verified in code)
- Safe because old tiebreaker continues being disallowed to be leader until removed
- Temporarily having 2 monitors in tiebreaker zone is acceptable
FIX STATUS: Closed via support guidance. Procedure documented in JIRA comments. No code fix needed -- documentation gap.

IBMCEPH-14348.analysis:
SUMMARY: RFE to support online BlueStore fsck on a running OSD without requiring OSD shutdown.
ROOT CAUSE: ceph-bluestore-tool fsck requires exclusive access to the BlueStore instance, meaning the OSD must be stopped. In production, stopping an OSD triggers PG remapping, backfill, temporary data unavailability, and performance degradation. This makes proactive or diagnostic fsck workflows expensive and disruptive. The customer experienced OSD failures on OCP 4.18.30 with Ceph 8.1z4 where PGs went undersized and impacted client IO, motivating the need for non-disruptive integrity checks.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- Customer environment: OCP 4.18.30, FDF 4.18.15, Ceph 19.2.1-292.el9cp (8.1z4)
- OSD downtime causes PG remapping and backfill
- Related clone: IBMCEPH-14349
- No comments or engineering response yet
FIX STATUS: Status 'new'. No fix timeline. Assigned to Adam Kupczyk. This is a significant architectural change requiring safe concurrent access to BlueStore data structures.

IBMCEPH-14368.analysis:
SUMMARY: OSD.40 crashed with ceph_abort() in build_incremental_map_msg due to BlueStore CRC checksum errors indicating hardware-level data corruption.
ROOT CAUSE: The OSD's BlueStore data on NVMe was corrupted -- blocks that should contain inc_osdmap.306 and osdmap.306 were zeroed out (CRC=0x6706be76 = CRC of all-zeros block). When the OSD attempted to share map epoch 306 during heartbeat, it could not load the incremental or full OSD map from its local store, triggering the panic/abort fallback path at OSD.cc:1484. The abort is expected behavior when neither incremental nor full map can be loaded. Brad Hubbard's analysis confirms this is a hardware issue -- the consistent 0x6706be76 checksum across multiple reads indicates the storage returned zeros where valid data should exist, pointing to NVMe write cache failure or firmware bug.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- 32 CRC errors in crash_dump_log.txt, all with calculated checksum 0x6706be76 (zeros)
- Crash at OSD.cc:1484 in panic path of build_incremental_map_msg()
- OSD was only 17 minutes old at crash time
- No power loss or failure simulation was running
- Hardware: Samsung MZ1L2960HCJR NVMe SSD on Intel Xeon 6710E
- Syslog kernel messages showed I/O errors around crash time
FIX STATUS: Not a software bug. Hardware issue on specific NVMe device. OSD marked down, priority lowered. Dev recommends HW investigation/replacement.

IBMCEPH-14388.analysis:
### Root Cause Analysis:
```
SUMMARY: Increased CPU utilization on RGW nodes after upgrade to 9.0z2, caused by active sync threads on single-site cluster
ROOT CAUSE: The cluster had residual multisite sync configuration from a previous setup. After upgrading to 9.0z2, rgw_run_sync_thread (default: true) caused RGW to continuously process data_log entries, generating high RADOS operation rates and PG log churn. The commit 37c1522bb39 ('rgw/sync: track last_update timestamp per-shard instead of per-entry') may have changed sync processing behavior, amplifying the CPU impact. Disabling sync threads resolved the issue: ceph config set client.rgw.${id} rgw_run_sync_thread false.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- CPU jumped from ~7% idle to 23-32% idle after upgrade
- Significant data_log.* activity across multiple PGs
- Multiple pg_update_log_missing errors (-61 ENODATA)
- rgw_run_sync_thread=true on single-site cluster with residual multisite config
- CPU normalized after disabling sync threads
- Two customers reported same issue
FIX STATUS: Closed (DONE). Not a regression — operational issue from residual multisite config. Workaround: disable sync threads on single-site clusters.
```

IBMCEPH-14392.analysis:
SUMMARY: Grafana certificate replacement via config-key commands fails on Ceph 9.x -- docs outdated, certmgr required.
ROOT CAUSE: Starting from Ceph 9.0, all TLS certificate management was moved from the legacy 'ceph config-key set mgr/cephadm/grafana_key' and 'mgr/cephadm/grafana_crt' mechanism to the new cephadm certificate manager (certmgr). The customer followed the old IBM documentation which still referenced the config-key approach. The old commands silently succeed (the keys are stored) but cephadm regenerates the Grafana config with its internal CA certificate on redeploy, ignoring the config-key values. The IBM Grafana docs were confirmed to be outdated/incorrect by Redouane Kachach.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- Customer used: ceph config-key set mgr/cephadm/grafana_key -i privkey.pem (old method)
- After ceph orch reconfig grafana, self-signed cert from internal CA still displayed
- Redouane Kachach: 'starting from 9.0 all certificates must be managed by cephadm certmgr'
- Correct commands: ceph orch certmgr cert set --cert-name grafana_ssl_cert --hostname <host> -i certificate.pem
- Existing docs ticket already open for correction
FIX STATUS: Documentation issue. Assigned to Vivek Maurya. The fix is to update IBM docs to reference certmgr commands instead of config-key. No code change needed. Should potentially be closed and tracked under the existing docs ticket.

IBMCEPH-14403.analysis:
SUMMARY: OSD crash loop during startup due to missing OSDMap epoch causing assert failure in prime_merges().
ROOT CAUSE: During OSD::init(), the OSD calls OSDShard::prime_merges() which needs to load a historical OSDMap (epoch 7455). The OSD's local OSDMap store returns 0 bytes for that epoch, meaning the map was either never persisted, was trimmed prematurely, or was corrupted. The code path in OSD.h:689 calls get_map(epoch_t) which asserts on the returned pointer (ceph_assert(ret)), causing an immediate abort. All OSDs on node bruuni010 are affected, entering a crash-restart loop. The missing map epoch is needed to determine PG merge state for PGs that were split/merged around that epoch.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- Crash in OSDShard::prime_merges() -> OSD::init() -> OSDService::get_map(epoch_t)
- Error: 'osd.0 7496 failed to load OSD map for epoch 7455, got 0 bytes'
- Assert: FAILED ceph_assert(ret) at OSD.h:689
- Version: ceph 20.2.1-252.el9cp (Tentacle 9.1)
- All OSDs on bruuni010 affected
- Core dump uploaded
FIX STATUS: Status 'new'. No engineering response yet. Core dump available for analysis. Assigned to Prashant Dhange. Potential fix: graceful handling of missing historical OSDMaps during prime_merges instead of hard assert.

IBMCEPH-14409.analysis:
SUMMARY: MGR port list in 'ceph orch ps' grows with duplicate entries after repeated upgrades/downgrades.
ROOT CAUSE: During repeated MGR upgrades and downgrades, the port list for each MGR daemon in the cephadm inventory accumulates duplicate port entries (e.g., port 8765 repeated 30+ times). The root cause is that the port reconciliation logic in cephadm doesn't deduplicate when updating the daemon inventory after a redeploy. Each upgrade/redeploy cycle appends the daemon's ports to the existing list instead of replacing it. The ports are stored in config-key (mgr/cephadm/host.<hostname>) and accumulate across reconfigurations. Additionally, Raimund Sacherer identified that port state changes (enabling/disabling services) don't trigger port updates in the inventory -- only a full 'ceph orch redeploy' refreshes them.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- mgr.ceph-1 shows: *:9283,8765,8765,8765,...(34 times)
- config-key dump shows accumulated ports array in host inventory JSON
- Restarting services doesn't help
- Reporter (Raimund Sacherer) has a fix PR ready
- Related tracker filed for port state not reflecting service enable/disable
- Fix may already exist upstream (Bipin asked if it's in 9.2/9.1 branches)
FIX STATUS: PR submitted by Raimund Sacherer. The fix was reportedly already implemented via a separate upstream commit. Clarification pending on whether it's in 9.2 and 9.1 branches.

IBMCEPH-14428.analysis:
SUMMARY: OSD heartbeat ping times exceeding 226 seconds due to faulty network switch causing packet drops, resulting in false OSD-down events in HCI/DCN environment.
ROOT CAUSE: A faulty physical network switch was dropping packets on the interconnect between Ceph nodes in a TripleO HCI/DCN (Distributed Compute Node) environment. This caused heartbeat ping times to spike to 200+ seconds (far exceeding default osd_heartbeat_grace of 20s), leading MONs to incorrectly mark OSDs as down while they were still running. The OSDs reported 'Monitor daemon marked osd.X down, but it is still running' and 'wrongly marked me down'. The issue persisted for ~21 hours until the faulty switches were rebooted. etcd healthchecks also failed concurrently, confirming network-wide packet loss.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- Heartbeat ping >226s on both front and back interfaces
- OSD logs: 'Monitor daemon marked osd.268 down, but it is still running'
- sub_op_commit_rec delay: 90 seconds between first and second sub-op acknowledgments
- etcd healthcheck failures: 'connection refused' at same timestamp
- OVN agent ETIMEDOUT errors concurrent with OSD issues
- Resolution: customer rebooted DC switches, OSDs stabilized
- Ceph version: 14.2.22-128.el8cp (RHCS 4.3z1)
FIX STATUS: Closed as 'not a bug'. Root cause was faulty network switch hardware. Mitigation for future: increase osd_heartbeat_grace to 60s and osd_heartbeat_interval to 10s.

IBMCEPH-14448.analysis:
SUMMARY: MDS stuck in Replay state with 90GB uncommitted journal after upgrade to 8.1z5 due to client cap revoke delays during MDS scale-down causing internal heartbeat timeout.
ROOT CAUSE: During ceph orch upgrade to 8.1z5, cephadm scales down the multi-MDS filesystem to 1 active MDS before upgrading MDS daemons. This triggers subtree export from rank 1 to rank 0. A Ganesha NFS client (client.72745998) was slow to respond to cap revoke requests, preventing subtree freeze from completing. The export operation retried repeatedly without converging, causing the MDSRank thread to time out its internal heartbeat (15s threshold), which led to skipped beacons, MON marking MDS as laggy, and replacement with standby. The replacement MDS then had to replay 90GB of journal entries. Greg Farnum identified batch getattr operations potentially bypassing freeze operations as a contributing factor. The issue occurred despite all PGs being active+clean at the time of scale-down.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- 'heartbeat_map is_healthy MDSRank had timed out after 15s'
- 'Skipping beacon heartbeat to monitors; MDS internal heartbeat is not healthy'
- 'client.72745998 isn't responding to mclientcaps(revoke)'
- 'client_request currently failed to authpin, subtree is being exported'
- 'export_dir Starting export to mds.0' retried repeatedly
- Slow requests spiked to 111,927 during scale-down
- 504 OSDs, 106,560 PGs (~630 PGs/OSD), all active+clean at scale-down time
- Client 72745998 = Ganesha NFS on same node as MDS
FIX STATUS: Still assigned/open. Under active investigation by Venky Shankar and Greg Farnum. Suspected client-side bug in cap revoke handling or batch operation interaction with freeze.

IBMCEPH-14787.analysis:
SUMMARY: Documentation bug - RGW Keystone authentication guide includes obsolete nss_db_path step and has incorrect case for rgw_keystone_admin_domain.
ROOT CAUSE: The IBM Storage Ceph documentation for configuring RGW with Keystone authentication still includes Step 1 to set `nss_db_path`, which was needed for PKI/PKIz token validation using a local NSS database. PKI/PKIz tokens were removed from OpenStack years ago, making nss_db_path completely irrelevant. Additionally, the docs specify `rgw_keystone_admin_domain = default` (lowercase) but Keystone's default domain is `Default` (capital D) - this case sensitivity causes RGW to fail admin token acquisition with 401 Unauthorized.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- nss_db_path is not a valid Ceph config key in current codebase
- Successfully completed Keystone auth (HTTP 204) on Ceph Tentacle 20.1.0 without nss_db_path
- rgw_keystone_admin_domain case sensitivity: lowercase 'default' causes 401 Unauthorized
- Affects docs for IBM Ceph versions 5, 6, 7, 8, 9
FIX STATUS: In progress. Assigned to RIVKA POLLACK (docs). QE (Prachi Lasurkar) verified both issues and requested doc changes from version 8 onward.

Environment: IBM Ceph 8.1+ with OpenStack Keystone integration
1. Configure RGW with Keystone auth WITHOUT setting nss_db_path -- intent: verify it's unnecessary
2. Set `ceph config set client.rgw rgw_keystone_admin_domain Default` (capital D) -- intent: correct config
3. Verify RGW auth works: create a user via Keystone, access S3/Swift endpoint -- intent: confirm HTTP 204
4. Test incorrect case: `ceph config set client.rgw rgw_keystone_admin_domain default` -- intent: demonstrate failure
5. Verify RGW returns 401 Unauthorized with debug logs showing admin token failure -- intent: confirm case sensitivity
DIAGNOSTIC COMMANDS:

- curl -v against RGW endpoint with Keystone token

IBMCEPH-15015.analysis:
SUMMARY: Ceph container images contain private SSH key (id_rsa_drop.ceph.com) triggering compliance scan failures.
ROOT CAUSE: The file /usr/share/ceph/id_rsa_drop.ceph.com is a legacy SSH private key originally used by the 'ceph-post-file' utility, which allowed users to upload crash dumps and logs to drop.ceph.com via SFTP. The host was configured to only allow sftp file uploads (no shell access). David Galloway confirmed the service the key connects to is no longer in active use. The key is packaged into all Ceph container images (rook-ceph-operator, cephcsi-rhel9, ceph, ocs-metrics-exporter-rhel9) and triggers Twistlock compliance scan failures for private key presence. While not an actual security vulnerability (the key only provides write-only sftp access to a defunct service), it causes compliance failures for customers with strict image scanning policies.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- Twistlock scan report flagging /usr/share/ceph/id_rsa_drop.ceph.com in 5 container images
- David Galloway confirmed: key is for ceph-post-file SFTP upload to drop.ceph.com (now defunct)
- Marcus Watts: 'It's certainly not a security exposure for a random ceph install'
- Sage McTaggart: 'This is embarrassing for Ceph but has very minimal impact on our actual severity'
- The service is being replaced with HTTPS POST by EOY
FIX STATUS: New/Open. Low priority per security team. Sage McTaggart plans to submit upstream PR to remove the key. Target: 9.2 or 10.0. No upstream tracker created yet. Marcus Watts provided downstream PR instructions in latest comment.

IBMCEPH-15159.analysis:
### Root Cause Analysis:
```
SUMMARY: ceph-exporter missing from logrotate postrotate signal list causes log rotation failure
ROOT CAUSE: The cephadm-generated logrotate configuration file (/etc/logrotate.d/ceph-<fsid>) did not include 'ceph-exporter' in the postrotate killall/pkill command list. After logrotate runs, ceph-exporter continues writing to the old (rotated) log file because it never receives the SIGHUP signal to reopen its log file. KEY EVIDENCE:
- Postrotate section missing ceph-exporter: 'killall -q -1 ceph-mon ceph-mgr ceph-mds ceph-osd ceph-fuse radosgw rbd-mirror cephfs-mirror tcmu-runner'
- Upstream tracker #67851: missing logrotate rule for ceph-exporter
- Upstream tracker #68721: ceph-exporter terminates on SIGHUP instead of reloading
- Fix PR: https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/60488
FIX STATUS: Fixed. Downstream MR !1862 merged for 7.1z10 (ceph-18.2.1-398). Verified by QE. Closed as part of 7.1z10 release. Backports: IBMCEPH-15535 (8.1z7), IBMCEPH-15536 (9.0z3).
```

IBMCEPH-15666.analysis:
SUMMARY: RFE to expose PG rebuild/recovery duration as a Prometheus metric using existing pg_stats timestamps.
ROOT CAUSE: No direct Prometheus metric tracks PG rebuild time. Fields like last_clean, last_undegraded, and last_fullsized exist in pg_stats but are not exposed via Prometheus in a way that allows computation of rebuild duration. The PoC mgr module (PR #69245) demonstrated that last_undegraded and last_fullsized converge to the same timestamp as last_clean after recovery completes, making the naive approach (duration = last_recovery_complete - last_clean) unreliable. Additional fields (num_objects_misplaced, num_objects_degraded, num_objects_recovered, last_change) are needed for a close approximation.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- Apple customer requirement for durability metrics
- PoC mgr module: https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/69245
- Pseudo-code logic tested: is_vulnerable = state & (PG_STATE_DEGRADED | PG_STATE_UNDERSIZED)
- Testing showed last_undegraded/last_fullsized timestamps collapse to last_clean after recovery
- Long-term solution planned for Ceph 10 (~9-10 months)
- Interim approach: replicate logic in Prometheus/ceph-exporter
- Scalability concern: ~50K+ PGs × 10 records = large in-memory footprint
FIX STATUS: PoC delivered. Interim solution being evaluated by Prometheus/Frontend team. Full productized feature targeted for Ceph 10.

IBMCEPH-15676.analysis:
SUMMARY: Multiple RGW segfaults (128 crashes in 5 days) during delete operations in a multisite environment after upgrade to IBM Storage Ceph 9.9.0.2, caused by memory corruption in the async request processing path.

ROOT CAUSE:
The RGW crashes are caused by memory corruption within the asynchronous processing framework (coroutine/io_context_pool). During multi-object delete operations in a multisite environment, a race condition leads to use-after-free or double-free of request state objects (req_state). The crash occurs in `req_state::~req_state()` during object destruction after the request has been processed. Analysis by L3 (Swati Thombe) confirmed this correlates with the memory corruption fix addressed in IBMCEPH-14213, involving the same async processing path. Stack trace shows: tcmalloc::ThreadCache::ReleaseToCentralCache -> req_state::~req_state -> process_request, indicating heap corruption detected during memory management.

KEY EVIDENCE:
- 128 RGW crashes in 5 days, all segfaults in thread `io_context_pool`
- Customer confirmed crashes occur mostly on delete operations
- Multisite environment confirmed
- Duplicate of IBMCEPH-14213 (memory corruption in async processing)
- Hotfix applied from private-tserlin-ceph-9.0-rhel-9-hotfix branch
- Customer confirmed hotfix resolved the issue (2026-07-08)
- Fix included in IBM Storage Ceph 9.9.1.0

FIX STATUS:
- Status: Closed (duplicate of IBMCEPH-14213)
- Fixed in IBM Storage Ceph 9.9.1.0. Hotfix validated by customer.

IBMCEPH-15691.analysis:
SUMMARY: cephadm-agent daemon version displays as <unknown> in `ceph orch ps` because the VersionStatusUpdater class has no handling for the non-containerized agent daemon type.

ROOT CAUSE:
The cephadm VersionStatusUpdater class determines daemon versions by exec-ing into the daemon's container and querying the version. The cephadm-agent is intentionally not containerized — it runs as a native Python process to avoid container management overhead for every data push. Because the agent daemon type is not included in the VersionStatusUpdater's special-case handling (which already exists for NFS, iSCSI, Prometheus, Grafana, etc.), the version detection mechanism returns null, causing `ceph orch ps` to display `<unknown>` for both the VERSION and IMAGE ID columns. The fix populates the agent version from the cephadm version itself.

KEY EVIDENCE:
- Reproducible 3/3 on Ceph 9.1 (20.2.1-280)
- Root cause traced by Swati Thombe: VersionStatusUpdater missing agent daemon type handling (comment 2026-06-05)
- Agent is intentionally non-containerized to avoid start/stop overhead per data push
- Impact extends to upgrade verification — without version info, operators cannot confirm agent daemons were upgraded
- PR raised upstream, approved for 9.2 target (moved back from 10.0 after pushback)

FIX STATUS:
- Status: In Progress
- Upstream PR raised and nearly ready. Targeted for 9.2 release. Ceph Tracker Bug #77111.

IBMCEPH-15699.analysis:
SUMMARY: RGW SSL certificate upload via Dashboard fails with 500 Internal Server Error on IBM Ceph 9.0z2 due to field naming mismatch introduced by certmgr changes.

ROOT CAUSE:
In Ceph 9.0, the cephadm certmgr feature changed the internal key name from `ssl_cert` to `rgw_frontend_ssl_certificate`. The Dashboard's service edit flow on 9.0 passes the certificate through `ServiceSpec.from_json()` which calls `validate()`. During validation, when `ssl=true` and `ssl_cert` is empty (because the Dashboard used the old field name), the code attempts to parse `rgw_frontend_ssl_certificate` as a combined PEM. If only a certificate OR only a key is provided (not both), `parse_combined_pem_file()` returns incomplete data, causing `SpecValidationError("Failed to parse rgw_frontend_ssl_certificate field.")`. This is a 9.0-only regression; versions 9.1+ include the CertMgr UI which handles the new field correctly.

KEY EVIDENCE:
- Stack trace: `service_spec.py:1764 validate() -> raise SpecValidationError("Failed to parse rgw_frontend_ssl_certificate field.")`
- Aarti Dhikale confirmed: `ssl_cert` is not populated correctly at runtime due to the field name change (commit a59cb5b5e2be)
- Abhishek Desai: "The issue is specific to 9.0 cause the certmgr cephadm changed the key for ssl_cert to rgw_frontend_ssl_cert"
- Velmurugan R confirmed the issue is resolved in 9.9.1.0
- PR raised: https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/ceph/ceph/-/merge_requests/1893 (for 9.0)

FIX STATUS:
- Status: Closed (Done)
- Fix: Not needed for 9.1+; CertMgr feature in Dashboard handles this correctly from 9.1 onwards
- Secondary issue: CA trust store not mounted in ceph-mgr container (workaround: mount host CA trust store)

IBMCEPH-15751.analysis:
SUMMARY: `ceph orch hardware status` fails with TypeError because node-proxy cache receives malformed data (non-dict values) from Redfish when hardware reports null health status.

ROOT CAUSE:
The `is_error()` and `is_unknown()` functions in `inventory.py` assume a strict nested dictionary structure (`status['status']['health']`). When Redfish API returns null values for Health fields (e.g., `"Health": null, "HealthRollup": null`) on certain Dell hardware controllers (AHCI embedded controllers with no drives), the node-proxy cache stores malformed entries. Attempting `status['status']['health'].lower()` on a non-dict or None value raises `TypeError: string indices must be integers`.

KEY EVIDENCE:
- Traceback: `inventory.py:1906 is_error -> status['status']['health'].lower()` -> TypeError
- Dell Redfish data shows: `"Status": {"Health": null, "HealthRollup": null, "State": "Enabled"}`
- Fix already in 9.1 via PR #74749 (commit ce360a4a5f67): `get_node_proxy_status_value()` centralizes safe access
- Guillaume Abrioux: feature developed/tested on VMs, limited hardware validation
- Backport to 8.1 deemed unlikely due to merge conflicts

FIX STATUS:
- Status: Closed (Done)
- Fix: Available in 9.1 (PR #74749, commit ce360a4a5f67329b95a4b75bc7b5e59dc7633637)
- 8.1 fix: unlikely to be backported; customer advised to upgrade to 9.1

IBMCEPH-15793.analysis:
### Root Cause Analysis:
```
SUMMARY: RGW lifecycle (LC) processing stuck with 234 buckets in PROCESSING state, unable to complete
ROOT CAUSE: The RGW lifecycle processing is unable to complete its workload within the configured processing window. With 234 LC operations stuck in PROCESSING state, the issue appears to be a combination of: (1) insufficient parallelism for the scale of delete operations (millions of objects daily, 1-day retention), (2) possible LC shard contention with current shard count, and (3) a known RGW segfault in RGWIndexCompletionManager::create_completion() during object delete in LC cleanup (IBMCEPH-12966/IBMCEPH-14805, targeted for 8.1z7). Engineering recommended: expand LC window to 24x7, reshard LC shards to reset partition structure, and potentially increase shard count.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- 234 LC operations stuck in PROCESSING (184 from yesterday, 38 from today, 12 from 2 days ago)
- 7 threads per RGW instance, 8 RGW instances across 4 servers
- Users delete millions of objects daily, 1-day retention policy
- radosgw-admin lc process --bucket=<name> shows brief peak then stalls
- Known segfault IBMCEPH-12966 in LC cleanup path on 8.1z6
- Version: 8.1z6 (19.2.1-366)
FIX STATUS: In progress. Recommendations: (1) Change LC schedule to 24x7 (00:01-23:59), (2) Run 'radosgw-admin lc reshard fix' to clear stuck processing state, (3) Increase LC shard count, (4) Upgrade to 8.1z7 for segfault fix. Customer action pending -- site requires physical access.
```

IBMCEPH-15801.analysis:
SUMMARY: CephFS metadata damage after recovering incomplete PGs with osd_find_best_info_ignore_history_les=true -- not a CephFS bug.
ROOT CAUSE: After recovering incomplete PGs in the CephFS metadata pool using the dangerous flag --osd_find_best_info_ignore_history_les=true, the CephFS journal became corrupted, causing MDS crashes and filesystem damage. The MDS crash was at CDir.cc:374 (FAILED ceph_assert(lookup_exact_snap(dname, last) == 0)) when trying to create a stray directory inode (ino:0x606) that already had a dentry present -- likely residual from the corrupted journal. The damage manifested as: 1 filesystem degraded, 1 filesystem offline, 1 MDS daemon damaged, with multiple dir_frag damage entries. Recovery required journal reset (cephfs-journal-tool --rank <fs>:0 journal reset), data scan (cephfs-data-scan), and ultimately deletion of 2 damaged PVCs. This was not a CephFS code bug but a consequence of using a dangerous recovery flag that can produce inconsistent metadata pool state.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- MDS crash: CDir.cc:374 FAILED ceph_assert(lookup_exact_snap(dname, last) == 0)
- Triggered by recovering PGs with osd_find_best_info_ignore_history_les=true
- damage ls showed 12 dir_frag entries across 2 CSI volumes
- Recovery: journal reset + cephfs-data-scan + scrub recursive,repair,force
- Final resolution: customer deleted 2 affected PVCs, cluster returned to HEALTH_OK
- Greg Farnum: stray directory fragment issue, possible interaction with stray dir fragmentation
FIX STATUS: Closed as 'not a bug'. This was data corruption from using a dangerous recovery option, not a CephFS code defect. Recovery was successful via standard disaster recovery procedures.

IBMCEPH-15802.analysis:
SUMMARY: RFE to handle missing journal header in cephfs-journal-tool recover_dentries, allowing partial metadata recovery.
ROOT CAUSE: When CephFS journal header object (object 200.00000000) is missing or corrupted due to incomplete PG in the metadata pool, cephfs-journal-tool event recover_dentries fails with 'Header 200.00000000 is unreadable'. The tool unconditionally requires the journal header to proceed with dentry recovery. Without it, the only option is destructive journal reset + full metadata rebuild via data scan, which loses uncommitted metadata changes. The RFE requests best-effort recovery that can extract dentries from surviving journal event objects even when the header is absent.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- Error: '2026-06-09T20:16:06.290+0000 7f09a5246400 -1 Header 200.00000000 is unreadable'
- Triggered by incomplete PG in metadata pool (since recovered)
- Workaround: cephfs-journal-tool journal reset + backward scrub (data scan) -- involves data loss
- Environment: ODF 4.18.23 (OCP-based)
- Upstream tracker filed

IBMCEPH-15874.analysis:
SUMMARY: BlueStore allocator commands `fragmentation` and `score` both return the same JSON key `fragmentation_rating`, making output ambiguous for monitoring scripts.

ROOT CAUSE:
The `ceph tell osd.X bluestore allocator fragmentation block` and `ceph tell osd.X bluestore allocator score block` commands both emit their results under the key `fragmentation_rating`. This is a labeling inconsistency in the BlueStore allocator output code — the score calculation uses a different metric than fragmentation but reuses the same output key name. This confuses monitoring scripts and makes it impossible to distinguish between the two values without knowing which command produced the output.

KEY EVIDENCE:
- `ceph tell osd.1 bluestore allocator fragmentation block` returns `{"fragmentation_rating": 0.387...}`
- `ceph tell osd.1 bluestore allocator score block` returns `{"fragmentation_rating": 0.833...}`
- Fix merged upstream; backport to 9.1z and 8.1z approved by Bipin Kunal but under debate about baking time
- Upstream dev (Radosław Zarzyński) concerned about breaking existing scripts that depend on the field name

FIX STATUS:

IBMCEPH-15886.analysis:
### Root Cause Analysis:
```
SUMMARY: NFS mount point becomes read-only after cluster upgrade due to stale grace table entry causing infinite NFS4ERR_GRACE
ROOT CAUSE: After upgrading to 8.1z6, an erroneous entry 'node0' was found in the RADOS grace table alongside the valid 'nfs.fileserver1.0' entry. This caused a coordination deadlock: the running Ganesha instance (nfs.fileserver1.0) expected the non-existent 'node0' to also enter and complete grace. Since 'node0' never existed, the recovery epoch (rec) remained non-zero, rados_cluster_try_lift_grace() kept returning false, and grace period never lifted. All OP_OPEN operations returned NFS4ERR_GRACE indefinitely -- clients could list directories (READDIR doesn't require OPEN) but couldn't read/write files. The stale 'node0' entry likely originated from a pre-8.1z3 NFS cluster setup that was upgraded through multiple versions.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- Grace table dump: cur=425 rec=424, two entries: nfs.fileserver1.0 (E) and node0 (NE)
- Continuous 'check grace:reclaim complete(0) clid count(0)' every 10s -- grace never lifts
- Export 1 failed with EPERM from ceph_start_reclaim() (main.c:456)
- All OP_OPEN -> NFS4ERR_GRACE (code path: open4_validate_claim -> nfs_get_grace_status)
- rados_grace_lift() succeeds (ret=0) but rec != 0 prevents grace lift
- Workaround: ganesha-rados-grace --pool '.nfs' --ns fileserver1 remove node0
FIX STATUS: Resolved via workaround (remove stale grace entry + restart Ganesha). Unable to reproduce in QE (tried 8.0z2->8.1z3->8.1z6 upgrade path). Root cause is stale grace state from unknown pre-8.1z3 upgrade path. Closed as 'insufficient data'. Preventive: check grace table content before upgrades.
```

IBMCEPH-15903.analysis:
SUMMARY: Dynamic resharding not triggered for versioned buckets because the 'resharding' feature was never enabled in the zonegroup configuration (pre-dates feature introduction).

ROOT CAUSE:
The `enabled_features` field in the zonegroup configuration was introduced in Ceph Pacific (5.x). For clusters created on earlier releases, this field is NOT automatically populated during upgrades -- it remains empty. The customer's cluster was originally created before this feature existed, so `radosgw-admin zonegroup get` showed `"enabled_features": []`. Without the 'resharding' feature enabled in the zonegroup, dynamic resharding cannot be triggered regardless of object count. Additionally, reshard locks were held by other RGW daemons, complicating diagnosis.

KEY EVIDENCE:
- `radosgw-admin zonegroup get | grep enabled_features` -> `"enabled_features": []`
- Swati Thombe: "The enabled_features field was introduced in Ceph Pacific. For clusters created on earlier releases, this field is not automatically populated during upgrades"
- After customer enabled resharding feature in zonegroup: buckets resharded successfully and large OMAP warning cleared
- 34 RGW daemons with reshard lock contention visible in logs

IBMCEPH-16005.analysis:
SUMMARY: CephFS clone stuck in 'in-progress' state cannot be cancelled because clone tracking index is missing, preventing removal of orphaned subvolumes.

ROOT CAUSE:
A CephFS clone subvolume is stuck in 'in-progress' state with its tracking index (symlink in `/volumes/_index/clone/`) missing. When `fs clone cancel` is attempted, the `cancel_job()` function calls `get_clone_tracking_index()` which returns None because no index symlink exists. This triggers `VolumeException(-errno.EINVAL, "error canceling clone")`. Additionally, the parent subvolume's `.meta` file still has a `[clone snaps]` section referencing the orphaned clone, preventing snapshot removal. The root cause of how the clone got into this inconsistent state (missing index + stuck in-progress) is unknown.

KEY EVIDENCE:
- MGR log: `mgr.server reply reply (22) Invalid argument error canceling clone`
- `/volumes/_index/clone/` is empty (no tracking symlinks)
- `.meta` file of parent has `[clone snaps]` section referencing the stuck clone
- Resolution: manually `rm -rf` clone subvolume, then edit `.meta` to remove `[clone snaps]` section
- Rishabh Dave: "Running rm -rf <path-to-clone-subvolume> should fix that issue"

FIX STATUS:
- Status: Assigned (manual cleanup performed, underlying cause unknown)
- Resolution: Customer manually removed clone directory and edited .meta file

IBMCEPH-16019.analysis:
SUMMARY: Monitor crashes with assertion `ceph_assert(num_down_in_osds <= num_in_osds)` in OSDMap::check_health() when NEW OSD states cause inconsistent counting.

ROOT CAUSE:
The `OSDMap::check_health()` function asserts that the count of down+in OSDs must not exceed total in OSDs. However, OSDs in the NEW state (just added but not yet fully initialized) were not consistently handled across the counting functions. When concurrent OSD operations (add/remove/replace) create NEW OSD entries, the health check assertion fires because NEW OSDs can appear as both 'in' and 'down' depending on which function counts them. This causes MON crash loops, preventing quorum formation. The upstream fix (PR #64009) ensures NEW OSDs are excluded from the health check counting.

KEY EVIDENCE:
- Assert: `/builddir/build/BUILD/ceph-19.2.1/src/osd/OSDMap.cc:7295: FAILED ceph_assert(num_down_in_osds <= num_in_osds)`
- Upstream tracker: Bug #70869
- Fix PR: #64009 (backported to ceph-9.2-rhel-patches as commit c9126c2eb751)
- QE verified: reproduced on 20.2.2-124 (down_in OSDs + new OSDs > in_osds), fixed on 20.2.2-220
- Trigger: node replacement + concurrent OSD operations under degraded conditions

FIX STATUS:

IBMCEPH-16022.analysis:
### Root Cause Analysis:
```
SUMMARY: Cephadm agent silently fails when keyring is invalid because MGR returns HTTP 200 on auth rejection
ROOT CAUSE: When the cephadm agent has an invalid/corrupted keyring, the MGR rejects the metadata POST but returns HTTP 200 with the error message in the response body ('Got wrong keyring'). The agent only checks the HTTP status code, sees 200, and considers the POST successful. This means: (1) agent appears 'running' in ceph orch ps and systemctl, (2) no CEPHADM_AGENT_DOWN warning is raised, (3) host metadata silently goes stale. The failure is only visible by examining agent journal logs for 'Got wrong keyring' messages, which doesn't scale.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- MGR returns HTTP 200 even when auth fails (error in response body, not status code)
- Agent checks only HTTP status code, not response body
- Stale metadata with no cluster-level warning
- Reproducer: corrupt agent keyring -> restart agent -> still shows 'running'
- Version: 9.1z2 (20.2.1-290)
FIX STATUS: Open (new). Agreed as valid improvement (not blocker). Agent should detect auth rejection and MGR should return proper HTTP error code. Assigned to Kushal Deb.
```

IBMCEPH-16023.analysis:
SUMMARY: Customer OSD spec affinity mismatch after disk replacement -- not a bug.
ROOT CAUSE: Two OSDs (osd.10 and osd.24) were reassigned to the 'osd.all-available-devices' spec instead of 'osd.uaeplus' after disk replacement because the customer ran 'ceph orch apply osd --all-available-devices' which created/updated the catch-all OSD spec. The osdspec_affinity is written at OSD deployment time by cephadm during mkfs, and ceph-volume only passes it through. When disks became available again while the 'all-available-devices' spec was managed, cephadm declaratively created new OSDs under that spec. The 'uaeplus' spec has restrictive filters (rotational:1 for data, rotational:0 for DB), so if the replacement disks didn't match those criteria, only the 'all-available-devices' spec (data_devices: all: true) would accept them. Cephadm documentation explicitly warns against running '--all-available-devices' alongside custom OSD specs.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- ceph orch ls shows 2 OSDs under osd.all-available-devices (5d old) vs 46 under osd.uaeplus (11w old)
- ceph osd metadata osd.10/24 shows osdspec_affinity: 'all-available-devices'
- Customer confirmed they ran 'ceph orch apply osd --all-available-devices' on May 14
- Guillaume Abrioux (cephadm maintainer) confirmed expected behavior
- Adam King confirmed 'ceph orch osd set-spec-affinity' command exists for reassignment
FIX STATUS: Closed as 'not a bug'. Resolution: use 'ceph orch osd set-spec-affinity osd.uaeplus 10 24' to reassign, then remove or unmanage osd.all-available-devices.

IBMCEPH-16079.analysis:
SUMMARY: Cephadm intermittently fails to create OSD daemons for some devices because the OSD IDs are not present in osd_uuid_map at deployment time, causing deploy_osd_daemons_for_existing_osds() to skip them.

ROOT CAUSE:
During new OSD node addition, ceph-volume successfully creates LVM structures and registers OSDs in the CRUSH map, but cephadm's `deploy_osd_daemons_for_existing_osds()` skips deploying the daemon because the OSD ID is not yet in `osd_uuid_map`. This happens because there's a timing issue between ceph-volume registering the OSD and the mgr's osd_uuid_map being updated. The skip condition `if osd_id not in osd_uuid_map: continue` silently drops the deployment request at debug log level. 80% reproducible on IBM Cloud Acadia environment.

KEY EVIDENCE:
- Aarti Dhikale analysis: `osd.62` and `osd.63` skipped in `deploy_osd_daemons_for_existing_osds()` because not in `osd_uuid_map`
- MGR logs show "Deploying daemon" for osd.56-61 but NOT for osd.62-63
- LVMs exist and are ACTIVE: `ceph-volume lvm list` shows both OSDs
- Workaround: `cephadm ceph-volume lvm zap /dev/nvme4n1 --destroy` then `ceph mgr fail && ceph orch set-managed osd.default_drive_group`
- 80% hit rate on reproduction

FIX STATUS:
- Status: Assigned (Guillaume Abrioux)
- Under investigation; debug logs requested from customer
- Workaround: zap + mgr fail + re-manage OSD group

IBMCEPH-16134.analysis:
SUMMARY: Unable to delete an orphaned RBD volume because the CSI plugin keeps re-establishing watchers, and `rbd rm` hangs iterating 227.5 billion non-existent data objects due to missing object-map feature.

ROOT CAUSE:
The RBD image (csi-vol-a6e6b619) has a corrupted/inflated size of 954 PiB (227.5 billion objects) but only the rbd_header object exists at the RADOS layer — no data objects. The image was created without the `object-map` feature (only `layering` enabled), so `rbd rm` must iterate through all 227.5 billion potential object names, issuing RADOS delete for each (which returns -2/ENOENT). This process would take weeks/months. The CSI plugin (Rancher Kubernetes) continuously opens the image from different cluster nodes, re-establishing watchers that prevent deletion via the normal path. Blocklisting the watcher IP doesn't help because a new client instance on a different node immediately re-opens the image. The watcher IPs rotate between 2-3 cluster nodes that run the CSI plugin.

KEY EVIDENCE:
- Image size: 954 PiB (227.5 billion objects), only rbd_header exists at RADOS layer
- Features: [layering] only — no object-map
- `rbd rm` runs 26+ hours with no visible progress (iterating non-existent objects)
- Watcher IPs rotate between nodes (CSI plugin instances)
- Different client instance IDs (413500793 vs 413500798) confirm different processes
- Resolution: customer agreed to leave the stale image as-is

FIX STATUS:
- Status: Closed (not a bug)
- Customer accepted leaving the orphaned image in place.

During the major version upgrade from 8.1z3 (Squid/19.x) to 9.0z2 (Tentacle/20.x), changes in how cephadm handles RGW service specifications and SSL certificate configuration cause the upgrade orchestrator to interpret the existing RGW service spec as invalid. The cephadm upgrade process then removes the RGW daemons rather than upgrading them. This is specifically related to the new SSL certificate configuration mechanism introduced in Tentacle that is not backward-compatible with Squid-era specs.

KEY EVIDENCE:
- All RGW daemons removed during 8.1z3 -> 9.0z2 upgrade
- Related to spec file changes and SSL certificate config mechanism changes
- Customer: Apple (TS022191113)
- Clone of IBMCEPH-15746
- Closed as "won't do" for 9.0z (no more 9.0z releases); tracked in 9.2 and 9.1z

FIX STATUS:
- Status: Closed (won't do for 9.0z)
- Tracked for fix in 9.2 and 9.1z branches.

IBMCEPH-16176.analysis:
SUMMARY: RGW cluster-wide brownout with GetObject latencies reaching 350+ seconds (up to 10+ minutes per customer metrics), correlated with BLUESTORE_SLOW_OP_ALERT on osd.2233.

ROOT CAUSE:
A ~50-minute brownout affected 182 RGW nodes across 6 buckets. The worst-affected bucket (swe-diaglogs-prod-acos-b1-us-east-1, ~500M objects) experienced GetObject latencies up to 354 seconds in RGW logs (customer-side metrics showed up to 487 seconds). The cluster logs show BLUESTORE_SLOW_OP_ALERT on osd.2233 starting at the same time as the latency spikes, persisting for ~70 minutes. The high latencies are for large objects (600MB-800MB) being served via Hadoop/Spark clients. The brownout self-resolved around 09:00 UTC with no manual intervention. Engineering (Matthew Benjamin) noted there's no evidence of an RGW software defect — this appears to be a storage-layer performance event (BlueStore slow ops on a single OSD cascading to RGW read latency). The root cause may be hardware (NVMe/disk issue on osd.2233's host) or transient I/O contention.

KEY EVIDENCE:
- 182 RGW nodes affected in ~50-minute window
- Worst GetObject latency: 354s (RGW logs) / 487s (customer metrics)
- BLUESTORE_SLOW_OP_ALERT on osd.2233 during same window
- Self-resolved; no manual intervention
- All affected GET requests returned HTTP 200/206 (succeeded, just slow)
- Cluster: Ceph 18.2.1-229 (Reef), ~500M object bucket
- Not related to earlier CompleteMultipartUpload fix (March 18)

FIX STATUS:
- Status: New
- Under investigation. Likely hardware/storage-layer issue, not RGW defect.

IBMCEPH-16213.analysis:
### Root Cause Analysis:
```
SUMMARY: NFS/MDS I/O stalls after adding OSDs to a cluster with CRUSH zone topology
ROOT CAUSE: When new OSD hosts are added without proper --crush-location, they land in the 'default' root alongside existing datacenter zones. This creates an invalid CRUSH hierarchy where the replicated_rule (type=host) combined with stretch mode (barrier=datacenter) causes PG placement calculations to fail. In the reported case, 61.6% of objects were misplaced, 3222 PGs remapped, and MDS rank 0 had slow metadata IOs blocked >1266 seconds with requests stuck at 'failed to rdlock, waiting'. The MDS was unable to complete lookup/getattr operations because underlying RADOS operations were stalled by the broken CRUSH topology.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- 3222 remapped PGs, 61.615% objects misplaced after OSD addition
- MDS_SLOW_METADATA_IO: oldest blocked for 1266 secs
- MDS_TRIM: 489/128 segments behind on trimming
- Reproduced in VM environment: adding OSD host without --crush-location caused 353 PGs to go clean+peered (inactive)
- Recovery: 'ceph osd crush move <host> datacenter=DC1 root=default' resolved all stuck PGs
FIX STATUS: Not a bug -- operational/CRUSH topology issue. Prevention: use a separate 'root zonal' for production datacenters, leave 'root default' as safe landing zone. Validated by QE (Kinjal Dhaduk). Resolved as 'not a bug'.
```

IBMCEPH-16284.analysis:
SUMMARY: cephadm-preflight.yml unconditionally enables firewalld during RHCS 7->8.1 upgrade, causing cluster outage in environments where firewalld is intentionally disabled.

ROOT CAUSE:
The `cephadm-preflight.yml` playbook contains a task that unconditionally starts and enables firewalld on all nodes without checking whether the administrator intentionally disabled it. When firewalld starts with default rules, it blocks inter-node Ceph traffic (MON, OSD, MGR ports), causing a complete cluster network outage. This is a regression from RHCS 7 where the pre-check process did not modify the host firewall state. The fix requires adding a configurable variable (e.g., `cephadm_preflight_manage_firewall`) to allow skipping firewall management.

KEY EVIDENCE:
- Customer (Swisscom) experienced IPTV streaming disruption during pre-production upgrade
- Reproduced in lab: nodes with firewalld disabled get it force-enabled by preflight playbook
- Workaround confirmed by Swati Thombe: set `enabled: false` in the firewalld task as temporary measure
- Fix being tracked under IBMCEPH-13852 PR (under review)
- Reporter suggests: `when: cephadm_preflight_manage_firewall | default(true) | bool`

FIX STATUS:
- Status: New (PR under review)
- Workaround: Manually edit cephadm-preflight.yml to add `when: false` to firewalld task
- Related: IBMCEPH-13852 (configurable firewalld management)

IBMCEPH-16365.analysis:
SUMMARY: MDS crash in cap_imports assertion during client reconnect replay -- the original tracking issue for IBMCEPH-17490 and IBMCEPH-17491.
ROOT CAUSE: The remove_replay_cap_reconnect() function in MDCache.h:681 asserts cap_imports[ino].size() == 1 then calls cap_imports.erase(ino). During MDS restart, multiple clients (client_A and client_B) may hold caps on the same inode, creating entries cap_imports[ino][client_A] and cap_imports[ino][client_B]. When one client's journal replay finishes, the assertion fails because size() is 2, not 1. The upstream fix removes only the specific client entry rather than the entire inode entry, and deletes the inode key only when no entries remain.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- Detailed code analysis by Vivek Maurya confirming multi-client cap_imports scenario
- Assertion at MDCache.h:681 in remove_replay_cap_reconnect()
- 10 crashes across MDS ranks a and b between May 27 and June 28, 2026
- VMware/ODF deployment with odf-operator.v4.20.2
- IBM case TS022492417
- PR opened upstream (referenced in comment 2026-07-07)

SUMMARY: During large-scale OSD node expansion, cephadm fails to create daemon containers for some OSDs despite them being registered in the CRUSH map, leaving OSDs in a permanent down state.

ROOT CAUSE:
When many OSD nodes are added simultaneously (large expansion), cephadm's OSD deployment pipeline creates the OSD entries in the CRUSH map and OSD map (via ceph-volume lvm prepare), but fails to complete the daemon container deployment for a subset of OSDs. The ceph-volume logs show successful keyring creation and object store initialization, but the `unit.run` file is never created for the affected OSDs, meaning cephadm never spawned the actual daemon container. The MGR logs show `Requested missing service osd.XXX` errors, confirming the daemon was never registered with cephadm's cache. The failure appears to be a race condition or resource exhaustion during rapid parallel OSD deployment — with `osds_per_device: 2` on 12+ NVMe drives per host, cephadm attempts to deploy 24+ OSDs per host simultaneously. The 80% reproduction rate on large expansions supports a concurrency-related root cause. The workaround (zap volume, mgr fail, set managed) forces cephadm to rediscover and redeploy the affected OSDs.

KEY EVIDENCE:
- 16 OSDs down across 2 hosts in a 1152-OSD cluster after expansion
- ceph-volume logs show keyring creation but no subsequent container deployment
- No `unit.run` file created for affected OSDs; no osd.XXX directory under /var/lib/ceph/<fsid>/
- MGR logs: `Requested missing service osd.690` for all affected OSDs
- LVM volumes exist and are valid (confirmed via ceph-volume lvm list)
- Reproduces at ~80% rate on large expansions
- Workaround: zap + mgr fail + set-managed forces rediscovery

FIX STATUS:
- Status: Closed (done)
- Recovery procedure documented; root cause in cephadm's parallel deployment pipeline under investigation

IBMCEPH-16457.analysis:
SUMMARY: `ceph orch upgrade ls` fails with 400 Bad Request because cephadm's registry token parser doesn't strip whitespace from WWW-Authenticate header parameters returned by IBM Container Registry.

ROOT CAUSE:
IBM Container Registry (cp.icr.io) returns WWW-Authenticate headers with spaces after commas: `Bearer realm="https://cp.icr.io/oauth/token", service="registry", scope="repository:cp/ibm-ceph/ceph-8-rhel9:pull"`. The current `registry.py:get_token()` implementation splits the header by comma but doesn't call `.strip()` on the resulting key-value pairs. This produces parameter keys with leading spaces (` service`, ` scope`) which create malformed OAuth token request URLs, resulting in HTTP 400 from the registry.

KEY EVIDENCE:

- Swati Thombe: "current parsing logic does not trim these spaces, causing authentication parameters to be incorrectly interpreted"
- Stack trace: `registry.py:20 get_token -> r.raise_for_status()` -> HTTPError 400
- Fix PR raised upstream (Bug #77780)
- 8.1z backport version of the fix

IBMCEPH-16463.analysis:
SUMMARY: SMB small-file sync is extremely slow (~100 files/min) because CephFS subvolume has case-sensitivity enabled, forcing Samba to issue massive readdir calls for case-insensitive lookups.

ROOT CAUSE:
SMB protocol operates with case-insensitive semantics, but the CephFS subvolume was created with `casesensitive: true` (default). When Samba needs to open/create a file on a case-insensitive share backed by a case-sensitive filesystem, it must enumerate the entire directory to check for case-colliding names. This caused ~95 readdir syscalls per smb2_create operation. With millions of files, the stat cache (which showed 0 hits) was ineffective, making each file creation trigger thousands of readdir operations. Setting `--casesensitive=0` on the subvolume reduced readdir calls from 8M to 362 in a 5-minute window and improved throughput from ~0.6 files/sec to ~120 files/sec.

KEY EVIDENCE:
- Samba profile: smb2_create: 85,031 / syscall_readdir: 8,094,073 = ~95 readdir per create (case-sensitive)
- After fix: smb2_create: 190,320 / syscall_readdir: 362 = ~0.002 readdir per create (case-insensitive)
- `ceph fs subvolume info` confirmed: `"casesensitive": true`
- Anoop C S: "the CephFS subvolume must have case sensitivity disabled"
- Direct CephFS: 0.2s for 100 create/delete; SMB: 5.6s = 28x slower via SMB
- Customer confirmed: performance improvement was "very large" after fix

FIX STATUS:
- Status: Assigned (monitoring, fix is configuration)
- Resolution: Create new subvolumes with `--casesensitive=0` and re-migrate data
- No code fix needed -- this is expected behavior when misconfigured

SUMMARY: After upgrading from IBM Ceph 8.1 to 9.1, cephadm normalizes hostnames to lowercase in its inventory but service placement specs still reference uppercase names, causing all service apply operations to fail.

IBMCEPH-16552.analysis:
SUMMARY: Cephadm module crashes with 'dictionary changed size during iteration' due to race condition between spec store iteration and concurrent CLI mutations.

ROOT CAUSE:
The cephadm serve loop's `_find_orphans_to_remove()` function accesses `self.mgr.spec_store.active_specs` which builds a dict comprehension from `self._specs.items()`. If a concurrent CLI command (e.g., `ceph orch apply -i spec.yaml` or `ceph orch rm`) modifies the `_specs` dictionary while the serve loop is iterating, Python raises `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration`. The race window is microseconds wide. The fix wraps the iteration in a `list()` constructor to iterate over a snapshot copy.

KEY EVIDENCE:
- Traceback: `inventory.py:460 active_specs -> return {k: v for k, v in self._specs.items() if k not in self.spec_deleted}` -> RuntimeError
- Timothy Nguyen RCA: "the stored specs was changed during the serve loop's orphan daemon clean up, so likely a cli command...was ran"
- Customer (IBM Cloud Acadia): intermittent HEALTH_WARN, resolved by `ceph mgr fail`
- Fix PR: https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/70411 (wraps dict iteration in list())
- QE unable to reproduce despite multiple attempts with concurrent orch apply/rm loops
- Impact: control plane only, data path unaffected

FIX STATUS:
- Status: Post (fix merged to main, targeting 10.0)
- Workaround: `ceph mgr fail` to restart the cephadm module
- PR: #70411 (ceph:main)

SUMMARY: cephadm-ansible preflight playbook force-enables firewalld regardless of customer configuration, disrupting cluster communication.

- Trigger: sosreport collection (which invokes dump_tree)

IBMCEPH-16988.analysis:
SUMMARY: RGW returns HTTP 200 with correct Content-Length but never sends the response body when a GET request includes an Origin header on a bucket without CORS configuration, causing client to hang until timeout.

ROOT CAUSE: The bug is in the RGW CORS handling during S3 GET object operations. When both global CORS and bucket CORS are unconfigured, the code path executes `op_ret = std::min(temp_op_ret, read_global_cors_ret)`. `read_global_cors()` returns -22 (EINVAL) when no global CORS exists, and `read_bucket_cors()` returns 0 when no bucket CORS exists. `std::min(0, -22)` yields -22, which is stored in `op_ret`. Later, in the `send_data` phase, the condition `if (get_data && !op_ret)` evaluates `!(-22)` as `false` (since -22 is non-zero/truthy in C++), so `dump_body()` is never called. The HTTP headers (including a correct Content-Length) have already been sent, but the body is never written, causing the client to hang. This is a regression introduced between 20.1.0-221 and 20.2.1-294.

KEY EVIDENCE:
- Regression: works in 20.1.0-221, broken in 20.2.1-294
- RGW log: 'No global CORS or bucket CORS configuration set yet'
- RGW log: 'http status=200' with 0 bytes transferred
- Source code analysis in JIRA comment identifies exact line: `op_ret = std::min(temp_op_ret, read_global_cors_ret)` setting op_ret to -22
- Workaround confirmed: setting any CORS config on the bucket resolves the issue
- Fix MR opened for downstream + upstream PR, merged at commit 2c2436c1775cfd834c530132499a70bd871b367a
- Customer Inditex blocked: this bug prevents deployment of a prior critical hotfix (IBMCEPH-14213)
- Labels: Hotfix_requested, IBM_Customer_Issue
- Cloned to IBMCEPH-17745 for 9.1z backport

FIX STATUS: Fix merged. Commit 2c2436c1775cfd834c530132499a70bd871b367a. Downstream MR and upstream PR both merged per Ali Masarwe's comment. Status: ON_QA.

IBMCEPH-17050.analysis:
SUMMARY: RGW ghost object (HEAD=200, GET=404) caused by multipart upload completion exceeding rgw_mp_lock_max_time, creating a lock-expiry race with overlapping CompleteMultipartUpload requests.
ROOT CAUSE: Multiple overlapping CompleteMultipartUpload requests for the same upload ID ran concurrently. The completion operation took ~104 minutes (far exceeding rgw_mp_lock_max_time=1800s/30min), causing the CLS multipart lock to expire. When the lock expired, a second request acquired it and completed as a fresh overwrite, enqueueing tail objects for GC. The first request eventually completed too, logging 'WARNING: failed to unlock'. GC later deleted the tail objects, leaving a ghost object (HEAD returns 200 from head object metadata, GET returns 404 because tail objects are gone). A concurrent cluster-wide latency event (index pool migration) caused the extreme completion times that exposed this known race (IBMCEPH-13341).
KEY EVIDENCE:
- CompleteMultipartUpload took 1h43m (6239s) -- far exceeding 1800s lock timeout
- 9 CompleteMultipartUpload requests sent within 6 minutes for same object
- 'WARNING: failed to unlock' in RGW logs -- confirms lock race

IBMCEPH-17052.analysis:
SUMMARY: radosgw-admin gc process with --bypass-gc triggers SIGSEGV due to null pointer dereference on uninitialized GC object.
ROOT CAUSE: When `radosgw-admin gc process --include-all --bypass-gc` is invoked, the `need_gc` variable becomes false (because bypass_gc=1 makes `!bypass_gc=false`). This causes the storage driver to be initialized WITHOUT the GC subsystem (`gc = new RGWGC()` is skipped). Subsequently, `RGWRados::process_gc()` calls `gc->process()` where gc is nullptr, causing SIGSEGV. The command combination is semantically invalid (you cannot process GC while bypassing GC initialization), but no guard exists to reject it.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- Stack trace: RGWGC::process(this=0x0) confirming null pointer dereference
- Ceph version 20.2.1-294.el9cp (Tentacle 9.1)
- Also affects `radosgw-admin gc list --bypass-gc` (IBMCEPH-17543, marked as duplicate)
- Root cause confirmed via coredump analysis from both cephadm shell and host execution
- Two proposed fixes: (A) null check in process_gc(), (B) reject invalid combination early
FIX STATUS: In progress by Aarti Dhikale. Upstream PR raised covering both gc list and gc process. Both IBMCEPH-17052 and IBMCEPH-17543 addressed under single patch. Proposed as blocker for 9.2 but not blocking release.

IBMCEPH-17115.analysis:
SUMMARY: Cephadm fails to create OSD daemon containers for some OSDs on newly added nodes despite OSDs being present in CRUSH map.
ROOT CAUSE: Two bugs in cephadm OSD deployment: (1) get_osd_uuid_map(only_up=True) logic inversion caused newly-created-but-still-down OSDs to be incorrectly treated as already deployed, skipping daemon container creation. - Workaround: zap volumes, mgr fail, set managed

- Fix verified on 19.2.1-401.el9cp with osds_per_device: 2 test

SUMMARY: mgmt-gateway service enters infinite reconciliation loop on 9.9.1.0 due to missing CA certificate in NGINX config and dependency mismatch in cephadm.

IBMCEPH-17251.analysis:
SUMMARY: BlueStore accepts non-power-of-two values for compression_min_blob_size, causing OSD crashes during compression workloads.
ROOT CAUSE: BlueStore's pool configuration validation does not enforce power-of-two constraints on compression_min_blob_size, compression_max_blob_size, bluestore_csum_min_block, and bluestore_csum_max_block. Values like 10000 or 32000 are accepted without error but cause OSD crashes when compression code paths assume power-of-two alignment for blob splitting and checksum block calculations. This is a long-standing validation gap, not a regression.
KEY EVIDENCE:

- Power-of-two values (16384, 32768, 65536) work correctly
- OSD crashes during compression workloads (elbencho test with snappy compression)
- Upstream tracker and PR exist for the fix
- Workaround: only use power-of-two values
- Proposed fix: return -EINVAL for invalid values

IBMCEPH-17271.analysis:
SUMMARY: NFS upgrade from IBM Ceph 8 to 9 fails because qos_type config parameter is converted from integer to string format before NFS daemon image is upgraded, causing parse failure and daemon crash loop.
ROOT CAUSE: During upgrade from Ceph 8 to Ceph 9, the mon/mgr daemons upgrade first and convert the QOS configuration in the .nfs RADOS pool from integer values (e.g., `qos_type = 1`) to string values (e.g., `qos_type = "Per_Export"`). However, the NFS daemon is still running the old Ceph 8 image (nfs-ganesha 6.5) which expects integer values. When the NFS daemon is restarted as part of the upgrade, it reads the now-string-format config and fails with 'Expected a number, got a double quoted string', entering a crash loop with UPGRADE_REDEPLOY_DAEMON error.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- Log: 'Config File (qosconf-nfs...): Expected a number, got a double quoted string'
- Log: 'Error while parsing qos configuration' -> 'Error setting parameters from configuration file'
- Upgrade path: IBM Ceph 8 (19.2.1-292.1.hotfix) to IBM Ceph 9 (20.2.1-379)
- Customer: Acadia Denali (IBM Cloud)
- Fix: commit b30b1a75c192 in 8.1z8 release - delays config conversion until after NFS image upgrade
FIX STATUS: Fixed in 8.1z8 (build ceph-19.2.1-397.el9cp). Verified by QE (Manish Singh) - qos_type correctly changes from integer to string only after mon+mgr upgrade, and NFS daemon remains stable.

IBMCEPH-17412.analysis:
SUMMARY: Two distinct S3 upload failure modes: oversized single PUT exceeding rgw_max_put_size (HTTP 400) and multipart upload signature mismatch from truncated parts (HTTP 403).
ROOT CAUSE: The Watsonx.data Spark Streaming application exhibits two failure paths when writing to RGW on IBM Ceph 8.1z6 (19.2.1-366.el9cp). (1) HTTP 400 failures: Presto/Spark issues single PUT requests with CONTENT_LENGTH exceeding rgw_max_put_size (default 5GB). RGW logs show CONTENT_LENGTH=5829528110 (5.4GB) and 6934835077 (6.4GB) hitting ERR_TOO_LARGE (error code -2019). The client does not use multipart upload for these objects. Increasing rgw_max_put_size to 10GB resolved this path. (2) HTTP 403 failures: During multipart uploads, an intermediate part (not the final part) arrives with only ~8MB instead of the expected 32MB part size. RGW computes the signature based on the received body, which doesn't match the client's signature calculated for 32MB, returning ERR_SIGNATURE_NO_MATCH (op status=-2027). A proxy between Spark and RGW may be truncating the body. The client aborts the entire upload upon receiving 403.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- Failed PUTs show CONTENT_LENGTH > 5GB with err_no=-2019 (ERR_TOO_LARGE) and http_status=400
- Successful PUTs show CONTENT_LENGTH=33554432 (32MB multipart parts) with http_status=200
- Part 6 failure: 8389280 bytes (~8MB) instead of 32MB, causing signature mismatch
- Workaround confirmed: rgw_max_put_size set to 10GB resolves the 400 errors
- Client: Hadoop 3.4.0 aws-sdk-java/2.31.19 on RHEL 9 with OpenJ9 JVM
- Reproducer being developed by WatsonX data team
FIX STATUS: Under active investigation. Ashish Singh confirmed rgw_max_put_size increase fixes 400 errors. The 403 errors require understanding why intermediate multipart parts arrive truncated -- likely a proxy/load-balancer issue rather than a Ceph bug. Kyle Bader requested Content-length and x-amz-decoded-content-length headers for the failed request plus client-side Spark logs.

IBMCEPH-17450.analysis:
SUMMARY: Race condition in cephadm daemon inventory causes RuntimeError during NFS deprovisioning.
ROOT CAUSE: During NFS daemon deprovisioning, the cephadm module's describe_service() method iterates over the daemon inventory dictionary via cache.get_daemons_with_volatile_status(). Concurrently, the NFS removal thread modifies the same dictionary (removing daemon entries as they are deprovisioned). The dict comprehension at inventory.py:1502 iterates dm.items() while another thread deletes entries from dm, triggering Python's RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration. This crashes the cephadm MGR module, requiring a manual MGR failover to recover. The race is intermittent because it depends on the timing of describe_service() calls overlapping with daemon removal operations.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- Traceback shows RuntimeError at inventory.py:1502 in get_daemons_with_volatile_status() during dict comprehension
- Crash occurs in describe_service() -> get_daemons_with_volatile_status() path
- NFS deprovisioning logs show daemon key removal immediately preceding the crash (within same millisecond)
- Affected version: IBM Ceph 9 (20.1.0-185.0.hotfix.IBMCloud55.el9cp) on IBM Cloud Acadia
- Workaround confirmed: ceph mgr fail restores service temporarily
- Related to IBMCEPH-16552
FIX STATUS: PR submitted at https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/70897 (posted 2026-08-06). Fix likely involves making a copy of the dictionary before iteration or adding thread-safe locking around the inventory access.

SUMMARY: ganesha-rados-grace command times out (10s) during NFS service deployment, causing transient CEPHADM_APPLY_SPEC_FAIL (8.1z backport).

IBMCEPH-17466.analysis:
SUMMARY: BlueFS::truncate assertion failure (cut_off == p->length) during OSD startup caused by highly fragmented allocations with changing allocation unit sizes.
ROOT CAUSE: During OSD startup, RocksDB attempts to recover log files and triggers a BlueFS::truncate call. This causes OSD crash loop during the mount phase (OSD::init -> _mount -> RocksDB RecoverLogFiles -> WriteLevel0TableForRecovery -> BlueFS::truncate).

IBMCEPH-17491.analysis:
SUMMARY: MDS crash during cap reconnect replay due to assertion assuming single client per inode in cap_imports map (8.1z backport of IBMCEPH-16365).
ROOT CAUSE: During MDS restart/failover, multiple CephFS clients reconnect and send CLIENT_RECONNECT messages for capabilities they held. These are stored in cap_imports[ino][client]. The function remove_replay_cap_reconnect() in MDCache.h:681 asserts cap_imports[ino].size() == 1, assuming only one client has caps on any given inode. When two or more clients held caps on the same inode before the MDS restart, this assertion fails because the map contains entries for multiple clients. The code then calls cap_imports.erase(ino) which would remove all client entries, but the assertion aborts the MDS before reaching that line. The crash cascades between both MDS ranks (a and b) as they repeatedly restart and crash in the same path.
KEY EVIDENCE:
- Assertion: FAILED ceph_assert(cap_imports[ino].size() == 1) at MDCache.h:681
- Backtrace: MDCache::try_reconnect_cap() -> Server::reply_client_request() -> Finisher thread
- 10 crashes in rapid succession across both MDS ranks (a and b) between 2026-05-27 and 2026-06-28
- VMware/ODF environment with odf-operator.v4.20.2
- Clone of IBMCEPH-16365 (original bug) for 8.1z backport
- Upstream patch not yet merged per comment from Bipin Kunal (2026-08-13)
FIX STATUS: PR opened upstream (referenced in IBMCEPH-16365). The fix modifies remove_replay_cap_reconnect() to remove only the specific client entry and delete the inode entry only when no reconnect records remain. Moved out of current z-release; targeted for next z-release. 9.1z backport tracked in IBMCEPH-17490.

IBMCEPH-17524.analysis:
SUMMARY: RGW daemon crash loop due to use-after-free in LCOpAction_Transition during lifecycle processing - dangling const& reference to transition_action after orule destruction.
ROOT CAUSE: LCOpAction_CurrentTransition objects hold a `const transition_action& transition` reference into `orule.env.op.transitions` map elements. These objects are not deep-copied when picked by the LC workpool threads. When orule gets updated/destroyed during LC processing, the workpool threads still hold dangling references to freed memory, causing use-after-free. tcmalloc detects the invalid allocation attempt and aborts the process. This matches exactly BZ#2416700 fixed upstream by Casey Bodley (commit d1f31bcb3da) - changing `const transition_action& transition` to `transition_action transition` (deep copy).
KEY EVIDENCE:
- Customer cluster: 19.2.1-366.el9cp (IBM Ceph 8.1z6), multisite master zone with lifecycle policies
- GDB shows corrupted transition.storage_class: 'Cannot access memory at address 0x2e312f5054544820'
- Days field shows garbage: 1969368370 (freed memory pattern)
- Fix: change const& to value copy in rgw_lc.cc line 1330
- Cherry-picked into ceph-8.1-rhel-patches as commits 120d52586b and af1f9c16d3
